Font source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lxgw/LxgwWenKai/4becfb4d5cf0c92cfdb60a6e9b504bda43315325/fonts/TTF/LXGWWenKai-Regular.ttf
License source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lxgw/LxgwWenKai/4becfb4d5cf0c92cfdb60a6e9b504bda43315325/OFL.txt

The complete, unmodified upstream SIL Open Font License 1.1, copyright
notices, reserved font names and additional permission are retained in OFL.txt.
The TTF is an unmodified upstream file. No conversion or subsetting was done.

Required embedding option: pdfDoc.embedFont(bytes, { subset: false }).
Use the full font with @pdf-lib/fontkit 1.1.1 and pdf-lib 1.17.1. Runtime
subsets from fontkit 1.1.1 were rejected after actual rendering omitted
characters despite retaining extractable Unicode. The Noto CJK CFF candidate
was also rejected: subset rendering lost letters and full-font extraction
mapped digits to private-use code points. Rejected candidates and QA files
were moved to _qa/font-compatibility outside the runtime vendor directory.

Verified with PDF.js 6.4.299: English, Malay in Latin/Rumi script, simplified
Chinese and traditional Chinese text renders correctly and extracts as exact
Unicode after removing layout whitespace. This includes ASCII digits and
accented Latin text. Invisible OCR text extracts correctly and renders no ink.
Unicode AcroForm values survive save/reload, and flattened forms render and
extract correctly. No PDF.js warnings occurred in the verified full-TTF mode.
All 95 printable ASCII characters and all 983 Han characters in the site's
current Traditional Chinese catalogs have glyph coverage. All test PDFs were
created and checked in memory; rendering evidence is outside this directory.

Tradeoffs: this fallback uses a calligraphic Kai style rather than Noto Sans.
The font download is 25,928,940 bytes and the test PDFs are about 13.14 MB
because the complete font is embedded. It is not a complete Unicode font;
check each requested code point, especially rare Han, emoji and Arabic/Jawi.
Only Latin/Rumi Malay was verified. This asset task changed no dependencies.

The separately bundled @pdf-lib/fontkit is declared MIT. Its legal provenance
and canonical MIT terms are recorded in fontkit-LICENSE.txt. The upstream fork
publishes no standalone LICENSE or exact 1.1.1 source tag/gitHead; that gap is
recorded rather than attributing an unsupported source revision to the release.
